title: Senior's toolkit: packages on every distro
summary: apt-get, apt-cache policy, apt-mark hold, dpkg -S, dnf provides, rpm -qf, apk and signed-by keyrings.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: packages on every distro
steps.body: You will install, pin and investigate packages on Debian-family servers, RHEL-family servers and Alpine containers. These are the commands for each, and the forms that are safe in scripts.

toolkit.what: The script and Dockerfile form of `apt install`: `apt` is for people and warns that its output may change.
flags: always in the same `RUN` line, so the index is never stale
toolkit.example: apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends curl ca-certificates && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

toolkit.what: The installed version, the version that would be installed, and which repository each comes from.
Keeps a package at its current version during upgrades, for example a database or a kernel you have tested.
Which installed package owns a file, and which files a package installed.
flags: the same for packages not yet installed

toolkit.what: The RHEL, Fedora and Rocky equivalents: which package would provide a file, and which installed package owns it.
Alpine's package manager. `--no-cache` downloads the index for this command only, so nothing is left in the image.
flags: group build tools to remove them in one go
toolkit.example: apk add --no-cache --virtual .build-deps build-base && make && apk del .build-deps

toolkit.what: The current way to add a third-party apt repository: its key in `/etc/apt/keyrings`, trusted only for that one repository. `apt-key` is deprecated, and apt 3.0 (Debian 13, Ubuntu 25.04 and later) no longer has it.
flags: this key may sign only this repository
convert an ASCII key to the binary format
toolkit.example:
curl -fsSL https://packages.example.com/key.asc | sudo gpg --dearmor -o /etc/apt/keyrings/example.gpg
echo "deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/example.gpg] https://packages.example.com/apt stable main" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/example.list

steps.prompt: On a minimal Rocky Linux server, `dig` says `command not found`. You do not know which package ships it. What do you run?
steps.explain: `dnf provides` searches the repositories, so it finds packages that are not installed yet (here `bind-utils`). `rpm -qf` only knows installed files, and `apt-file` is the Debian tool. On Debian and Ubuntu the package is `bind9-dnsutils` (or `dnsutils`).

steps.prompt: `apt-get update` fails with `NO_PUBKEY 3B4FE6ACC0B21F32` for a vendor repository. An old blog post says `apt-key adv --recv-keys`. What do you do instead?
options: Download the vendor's key into `/etc/apt/keyrings/` and reference it with `[signed-by=...]` in that repository's line
Delete the repository and install the `.deb` by hand
steps.explain: `apt-key` trusted a key for every repository at once and is deprecated (removed in apt 3.0). `signed-by` limits the key to one source. `trusted=yes` turns signature checks off, which lets anyone in the network path feed you packages.

steps.prompt: Match each question to the command that answers it.
pairs: Which version would apt install, and from where?
Keep this package at its current version
Install curl in Alpine without leaving the index

steps.prompt: Install curl the image-friendly way on Debian and on Alpine.
steps.explain: `--no-install-recommends` skips optional packages that can double an image's size; `--no-cache` keeps Alpine's index out of the layer.

steps.prompt: Which family does each command belong to?

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: In scripts and Dockerfiles use `apt-get` with `-y --no-install-recommends` and `apk add --no-cache`. When a tool is missing, ask the package manager who provides it instead of searching the web, and add vendor repositories only with a `signed-by` key.
